title: Life Reset That Actually Works!
body:
I’ve tried a lot of productivity and goal-tracking apps over the years, but Priori: Life Reset is one of the few that actually feels different. The structure of the app makes it really easy to break down goals and stay consistent without feeling overwhelmed. I like that it focuses on neuroscience and building habits gradually instead of just throwing a bunch of tasks at you.

The interface is clean, simple, and motivating to use daily. It feels more like a system for improving your life rather than just another checklist app. If you’re trying to reset your habits, get organized, or focus your energy on meaningful goals, this app is definitely worth trying.

Highly recommend it for anyone serious about personal growth and staying accountable.

title: Feels like a motivational poster pretending to be an app
body:
Downloaded Priori expecting a productivity tool, but it’s basically a glorified to-do list with some buzzwords and cheesy pop psychology sprinkled in. It keeps asking me about my “top 3 life priorities” like it’s trying to be my therapist, then turns around and suggests goals like “drink water” and “take a deep breath.” Thanks, but I didn’t need an AI to tell me I’m dehydrated.

The interface is cluttered, the reminders are generic, and the “points” system feels like a participation trophy for adults. Nothing here actually helps you move forward. It’s just empty encouragement dressed up as productivity. Also, if you’re already overwhelmed, the app’s constant notifications will push you over the edge.

If you’re looking for something that genuinely helps you stay on track, look elsewhere. This app tries to be deep but ends up being deeply annoying.
